I have noticed many successful people across the video game industry employ a disclaimer similar to: "Tweets are my own" on their Twitter bio. I've been wondering if a disclaimer is necessary.

  • If you have questionable social media use that gets you in hot water at work, I doubt a disclaimer can help. Does such a warning carry legal protection?

  • It is not very visible. Most people just see your tweet or retweet and may not read through your disclaimer.

  • Are you not still a reflection of your brand image/company, even if you claim the information you disseminate reflects you as an individual?

What do you think about Twitter disclaimers for industry professionals?
How does /v/gamedev feel about Twitter disclaimers - "Tweets are my own"?

It's sad but necessary, especially in these lawyer-filled and common-senseless days. The truth of it is that the disclaimers protect one's employers more than they protect the poster, with regard to various potential torts. They're a lot less useful for someone who is a public face of an organization (PR, executives, big name employees) however, because those people are considered to be part of the org's brand unlike your run-of-the-mill company grunt.

With regard to actual legal protection, that'll differ from jurisdiction to jurisdiction, and anyone who wants to know how well adding one to their own Twitter account or other social network profiles would be best to consult a local lawyer with experience in tort law.
